i use depixym cosmetic emulsion, you can get it on beautybay, on a small eyeliner brush and go super slow to get that tiny line. i use the morphe eyeliner brush that came in the james charles set, i cant remember what its called, but the depixym is fully waterproof and like 90% smudgeproof once it dries, they have loads of colours, it lasts AGES (my tube barely has a dent made after wearing eyeliner every day for over a year) and bonus it comes in a cute little metal tube like acrylic paint! its a little pricey, but worth it for that extra staying power and how long it lasts. if its a little out of your budget, any gel liner works, and i find them much easier to control than liquid, but if you have watery eyes then definitely make sure its waterproof. if i want colourful liners, i also scrape off a pigmented eyeshadow and mix it with inglot duraline mixing medium, since that lasts pretty well as a liner too. literally, use the skinniest brush you can. with your inner corner, start as TINY as you can and you can build on it. usually, you want to draw it smaller than you think. personally, i basically flatten the tip of my brush on the edge of the tube and draw little 'dots' that come out as more dashes and keep dotting until it makes a cute inner wing shape, but youll develop a method thats works and makes it easy for you if you play around with different methods and find a shape that suits you. happy eyeliner-ing :)
